resources.string: Looking for a Switch 2 GameCube / Pro controller on USB…
Input report format sent by Start controller:
Standard gamepad (0x0A): Android and games see a gamepad

Peek claims the HID interface for 2 seconds to read raw reports. That detaches the kernel HID driver, so the gamepad disappears from Input devices while Peek runs. Android should reattach the driver when Peek ends; if the gamepad doesn\'t come back, unplug and replug the controller. Use it only when no gamepad input shows up, to see whether the controller is streaming at all.
Press a button or move a stick. Events from gamepads and joysticks show here.

Every controller Android knows (Bluetooth or USB) is logged while this screen is in front. Turn on Button capture to keep logging buttons while a game is in front; sticks and triggers need this screen, USB capture or Bluetooth capture.
The overlay needs \"Display over other apps\" for GC Bridge. Turn it on, then come back and tap Show overlay again.

An accessibility service that sees controller buttons in every app (not sticks or hat D-pads). Enable it under Settings › Accessibility › Installed apps › GC Bridge. On Android 13+ a sideloaded app is blocked until you allow restricted settings: App info › ⋮ › Allow restricted settings.
Button capture: enabled in Settings, waiting for Android to start it
Logs controller button presses for the GC Bridge overlay and recordings while other apps are in front. It never changes or blocks the buttons and reads nothing from the screen.
USB capture (GC Bridge reads the controller)

Reads the Switch 2 GameCube / Pro controller directly over USB-C: full analog triggers, 250 reports per second, works in the background. While it runs Android has no gamepad for this controller, so use it to log the pad by itself, not while a game on this phone needs it. Stop it (or replug) to get the gamepad back.

Connects to a Switch 2 GameCube / Pro controller over Bluetooth LE without pairing and reads its reports for logging and the overlay. Android itself never sees a gamepad this way. Hold the controller\'s SYNC button until its LEDs run back and forth, then tap Scan. Never pair it in Android\'s Bluetooth settings (that makes it disconnect).
This device has no Bluetooth LE.
No recordings yet. Tap Record, press some buttons, then Stop recording.
Files are in Android/data/com.controllerlog.gcbridge/files/recordings (visible from a PC over USB) and open with \'controllerlog view\' on the PC.
Shown while GC Bridge records input or shows the overlay.
